sources.name: The Straits Times via Red Hot Singapore

caption:
Meta says a tool built on Anthropic's Claude triggered the suspension of the No Kings Coalition's Instagram account during its Oct. 17 day of action.
Meta says the tool read profiles, posts and hashtags at about four times the normal rate, which looked like bot traffic.
Meta has apologized, but has not said who ran the tool.

Should platforms be able to tell an AI agent from a bot?

slides.headline: Meta just blamed *Claude* for knocking a protest group off Instagram

slides.heading: Dark during *3,000 events*
paras: The No Kings Coalition's Instagram account went dark around 1:30 p.m. Eastern on Oct. 17, during a day of action with nearly 3,000 planned events.
Public access came back about 90 minutes later. Organizers say it took hours more before they could manage the account again.

slides.heading: Meta points at *Claude*
paras: Meta says a tool built on Anthropic's Claude was reading Instagram profiles, posts and hashtags at about four times the normal rate, in intense bursts.
Meta communications VP Andy Stone said the requests "resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems."

slides.heading: The *questions* Meta left open
paras: Meta has not said which Claude-based tool was running, who operated it, or how it was linked to the No Kings account.
Meta first blamed high-frequency posting. Organizers pushed back, saying they posted only a few times and mostly livestreamed rallies.

slides.heading: A rare *apology*
paras: "We want to reiterate our sincere apology for the error," Stone wrote. Meta says the account is now working normally.

paras.t: The coalition, which includes groups like Indivisible and the ACLU, called the suspension unjustified and asked Meta for more transparency.

slides.hook: An AI tool just set off Meta's bot alarms on a protest account. Follow to see what Meta and Anthropic say next.
